newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Gold-Price fall comes amid high costs.
newsitem.headline: Australia Gold-Price fall comes amid high costs.

text.p: The most recent decline in the gold market overnight arrived as Australian gold producers were coming to terms with higher cash operating costs.

"The seasonal impact of the rainy season and cyclones that affect the northern half of Australia exerted their usual dampening effect on the March 1997 quarterly results, with the annualised rate falling back to 285 tonnes a year at one percent higher cash costs of A$371 an ounce," Bell Securities analyst Keith Goode said in a report.

Overall, Australia has the highest production costs in the industry, owing to an unfavourable exchange rate against the U.S. dollar and declining grades from deeper pits, Gold Fields Mineral Services Ltd noted earlier this month.

Metals dealers said a US$2-plus in bullion prices on Wednesday due in part to concerns that Germany was considering using some Bundesbank gold reserves for budgetary purposes has done little to endear investors to gold stocks.
"The Germans never actually said they were going to sell gold but still the price goes down," one said. "How do you combat that?"
Analysts noted a newspaper report did not say Germany would actually sell gold outright, only that the gold reserves would be revalued to market prices and used to finance "investments."
Nevertheless, local dealers said it was unlikely Australian gold producers would find much reason to sell gold in the current climate.
"There are some support levels in the low-to-mid-forties (US$340-$345 an ounce range) that should keep any declines in check," a dealer at a bank said.
